# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

No existing project. We need to build a game. Given time constraints, a self-contained HTML/canvas game with rich mechanics would be best. Could use Three.js for 3D? "Spore but better, more mutations genes and evolution, better more detailed map and graphics, breeding and den/shelter building after certain perk or evolution is reached". 

Options:
1. 2D top-down evolution survival game with canvas, procedurally generated detailed map, day/night, weather, biomes, creatures, DNA, mutations, breeding, den building. This is achievable and can look quite good with canvas rendering + shaders-ish effects. 
2. 3D with Three.js. More impressive graphics but much more work and risk.

A rich 2D top-down game can be visually detailed: layered terrain with noise, grass, trees, water with animated ripples, particles, lighting. Evolution stages: microbe -> amphibian -> land creature -> apex. Mutations gene system with tiers, perk tree. Breeding with genetic inheritance. Den building with materials and shelter mechanics. Ecosystem simulation.

But "Spore but better" implies cell stage to creature stage plus evolution. We can make a cohesive 2D game across eras: Tidepool (cell), Shore (amphibian), Savannah/forest (creature), maybe tribal? Too much. Focus on a deep creature survival game with evolution phases.

Let me design:

**Title: SPORELING — Evolution Unleashed** or "GENESIS: Spore-like". Let's name it "ABYSS TO APEX" or "Spore: Genesis". Maybe "EVOLVE: Genesis".

Core loop:
- You control a creature in a procedurally generated world.
- Eat food, avoid predators, gain DNA/EP, level up, unlock mutations.
- Mutations grouped in genes: body (size, speed, armor, attack, senses), metabolism, social, special (venom, camouflage, glide, burrow, fire?).
- Each mutation has tiers and visual effect on your creature sprite (procedural body segments, horns, fins, eyes, spikes, wings).
- Evolution stages: Microbe -> Larva -> Crawler -> Beast -> Apex. Reaching stage milestones unlocks new abilities and world content.
- Breeding: once you have "Nest Instinct" perk/evolution, you can build a den/shelter. Den gives safe storage, heals, allows mate/breeding, offspring inherit mixed genes with mutations. You can play as offspring or keep parent.
- Den building: gather materials (wood, stone, fiber, crystal), build and upgrade den modules (nest, walls, food storage, incubator, shrine). 
- World: biomes (shallows, marsh, forest, savannah, ashlands, crystal grove), day/night, weather (rain, fog, storm), rivers, ponds, cliffs, caves. Map minimap and full map overlay. Detailed graphics: procedural terrain with layered noise, animated water, swaying grass/trees, lighting from sun/moon, particles, bloom via canvas composite maybe.

Need touch support (per Agents.md mobile browser games). Add joystick and buttons.

Tech: plain HTML/CSS/JS with canvas. No build deps. Single index.html plus modules? Since default-start serves static files directly, we can use ES modules without bundler if index.html exists and type=module. But file loading over HTTP works fine. We'll use vanilla JS modules. Simpler: one big game.js plus styles. But maintainability matters; however a single file is easier to ensure no errors. Maybe split into modules: main.js, world.js, player.js, mutations.js, ui.js, etc. Can use ES modules served statically.

However capture may run with strict; need no console errors, mobile support.

Let's plan a robust architecture:

- index.html: canvas + overlay UI built with DOM for HUD, menus, mutation tree, breeding, build, map, journal, settings. CSS rich styling.
- game.js (~2000+ lines): game engine.

Rendering:
- Canvas 2D with camera following player. World size ~4000x4000 (or 6000). Procedural terrain via value noise (seeded), pre-rendered to offscreen canvases in chunks for performance. Chunks 512px, generated on demand, drawn with grass texture details (thousands of small blades), rocks, trees, flowers, ponds.
- Water bodies: define water mask from noise; animated overlays? Pre-render water base but animate with sine lines drawn per frame near camera. Simpler: render water in chunk with wave pattern; add animated sparkles particles.
- Day/night: overlay color multiply and light glows. Fireflies at night. Sun shafts? Keep tasteful.
- Creatures: procedural drawing function based on genome traits, with animation (walk bob, tail sway). Player with distinct colors, NPC creatures with species traits. Predators, prey, neutral. AI wandering, fleeing, hunting.
- Particles: dust, splash, blood?, pollen, rain.
- Shadows.

Gameplay details:
Stats: Health, Stamina, Hunger, Thirst? Keep hunger + health + stamina + temperature maybe. Simpler: Health, Energy (stamina), Food (hunger), DNA points. Plus "Evolution Points" (EP) used to unlock genes, DNA used to buy mutations? Let's define:
- Biomass (food) fuels growth/hunger. Eating restores hunger.
- DNA earned from eating, discoveries, surviving, breeding, exploring. DNA spent on mutations.
- Evolution level XP unlocks tiers/stages.

Mutations: ~30+ genes across 5 categories with tiered upgrades (maybe each gene has up to 3 ranks) = lots.
Categories:
1. Body: Size, Speed, Armor (carapace), Strength (jaws), Regeneration, Wings/Glide, Fins/Swim, Claws, Spikes.

hash2 needs integer coords; use Math.imul.

```js
export function hash2(x, y, seed = 0) {
  let h = Math.imul(x | 0, 0x27d4eb2d) ^ Math.imul(y | 0, 0x165667b1) ^ Math.imul(seed | 0, 0x9e3779b1)
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 15), 0x85ebca6b)
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 0xc2b2ae35)
  return ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
}
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable "Spore but better" evolution survival game with more genes/mutations, detailed map/graphics, breeding, and den/shelter building unlocked by a perk/evolution, plus additional fun systems.

## Requirements
- Build now, no clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when finished.
- Existing repo had no game; static `index.html` is served by the default runtime.
- Support desktop and mobile/touch controls.

## Decisions
- Built a custom 2D canvas top-down evolution survival game titled **SPORE GENESIS** using vanilla ES modules (no bundler/dependency install).
- Core systems: 30 genes across 5 categories with ranks/stage gates, 5 evolution stages, procedural 6400×6400 world with 10 biomes/chunks/day-night/weather, breeding with inherited genes and heir companions, den construction with 7 upgradable modules, quests, achievements, map/fog-of-war, minimap, save/load, procedural audio, keyboard/touch input.
- Title screen has exactly one auto-capture-eligible button labeled `Start`; `New Game` is deliberately non-matching.
- Assumption: player starts as a small land creature; "Spore-like" progression is represented by five creature evolution stages rather than literal cell/tribal phases.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` created with HUD, panels, title/death overlays, mobile controls, script entry.
- `styles.css` created with full responsive desktop/mobile styling.
- `src/util.js` created (noise, RNG, color, math helpers).
- `src/data.js` created (biomes, stages, 30 genes, den modules, species, quests, achievements, derived stats).
- `src/world.js` created (procedural terrain, chunks, biomes, harvestable objects, object drawing, collisions, map base).
- `src/creature.js` created (procedural creature phenos and detailed animated rendering).
- `src/game.js` partially written: imports/constants/Sound; Game constructor/boot/new game/load/save/serialize/recalc/start; main loop, resize, idle/update/time/weather/player updates; feedback helpers; NPC spawning/AI/companions/mate/den/corpses/clouds/exploration/progression; all player actions/combat/interaction/breeding/den building/rest; most rendering (world layering, creatures, den, corpses, particles, slashes, clouds).
- Appended `src/game.js` in chunks successfully through `drawSlashes`.

### Active
- `src/game.js` is incomplete and not yet syntactically validated. Still missing:
  - `drawLighting`, `drawWeather`, `drawVignette`
  - minimap/map pixel rendering and big map
  - `updateHUD`, `updatePrompt`, avatar update
  - all panel renderers (`renderMutations`, `renderBuild`, `renderBreed`, `renderJournal`, `renderMapPanel`, `renderPause`)
  - panel actions/open/close logic
  - `bindUI` (keyboard, mouse, joystick, touch buttons, title/death buttons)
  - final boot invocation (`new Game().boot()` or equivalent)
  - `updateParticles` must also update `this.floaters` (currently omitted).
- No browser run/screenshot/test has been performed yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Append remaining rendering methods to `src/game.js`: lighting/day-night, rain/fog/lightning, vignette, map/minimap drawing.
2. Append HUD/prompt/avatar updates and all panel renderers plus event/action handlers (`bindUI`, open/close panels, mutation buying, den modules, breeding, rest, journal, map, pause, save/new game).
3. Add boot entrypoint; patch `updateParticles` to update floaters.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “Spore but better” evolution survival game with more genes/mutations, detailed map/graphics, breeding, den/shelter building unlocked by a perk, and additional fun systems.

## Requirements
- Build now, no clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when finished.
- Game is served as static HTML from repo root `index.html`.
- Support desktop and mobile/touch controls.
- Capture auto-clicks only one visible button matching `/^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i`; keep `Start` as the only eligible title button.
- Screenshots are taken 1 second after auto-start at 1440×900 and 390×844; title must disappear immediately on Start.

## Decisions
- Built custom 2D canvas top-down evolution survival game **SPORE GENESIS** using vanilla ES modules, no bundler/deps.
- Core systems: 30 genes across 5 categories with ranks/stage gates, 5 evolution stages, procedural 6400×6400 world with 10 biomes/chunks/day-night/weather, breeding with inherited genes and heir companions, den construction with 7 upgradable modules, quests, achievements, map/fog-of-war, minimap, save/load, procedural audio, keyboard/touch input.
- Assumption: player starts as a small land creature; Spore-like progression represented by five creature evolution stages rather than literal cell/tribal phases.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` built with HUD, panels, title/death overlays, mobile controls, module entrypoint.
- `styles.css` built with full desktop/mobile styling, including panel, gene, den, breeding, journal, map, pause, and creature-preview styles.
- `src/util.js`, `src/data.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/creature.js` completed.
- `src/game.js` completed through all simulation, rendering, UI, panel, input, and bootstrap systems; syntax validated.
- Added and wired: day/night lighting, rain/fog/lightning weather, vignette, minimap, big map with fog-of-war, HUD/prompt/avatar updates, mutation/build/breed/journal/map/pause panels, gene purchase, keyboard/mouse/virtual joystick/touch controls, save/load, death/respawn.
- Fixed major structural bug: extra class-closing brace had made all methods after `enterWorld()` top-level calls; removed it.
- Fixed `stepNPC` optional `species`, companion/mate save-load radius/size fields, `this.genes` → `this.player.genes`, and panel-open simulation skipping.
- Improved terrain rendering: increased chunk base grid from 32 to 64 cells and smooth upscaling; blocky terrain now much softer.
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html` to prevent favicon 404.
- Browser testing passed: title, Start, desktop/mobile gameplay, gene purchase, stage evolution, eating, drinking, quest progression, den founding, Brood Nest construction, mate spawning/courtship, breeding, journal, map, pause, death/respawn, touch interact, touch attack, virtual joystick, storm weather.
- Mobile layout fixes: moved menu buttons below DNA card; moved toasts above quest; moved prompt lower to avoid quest overlap.

### Active
- Final visual/UX polish and end-to-end verification are ongoing.
- `capture.sh`/default capture has not yet been run; favicon fix still needs a reload verification.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the browser after the favicon change and confirm console has no application errors.
2. Re-test mobile gameplay/prompt spacing after CSS prompt adjustment.
3. Run `capture.sh` with `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002` and a capture output directory; inspect `final-desktop.png` and `final-mobile.png`.
4. Verify no unintended extra auto-start-eligible button is visible on the title screen.
5. Test night lighting, den rest, additional den modules, quest chain completion, and save/load after a fresh page reload.
6. Perform final `node --check` on all JS modules and review git diff; commit if requested.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: main game controller; completed, highest-priority file.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM IDs/panels/title overlays; now includes favicon link.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all UI styling; recent mobile layout fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: procedural terrain, chunk smoothing change.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: genes, biomes, species, modules, quests, `deriveStats`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js`: creature phenos and preview rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/util.js`: math/noise/color helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/favicon.svg`: new icon asset.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: runs default screenshot capture.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: serves static `index.html`; currently running via tmux session `spore` on port 3002.

## Important Context
- Server is running at `http://localhost:3002` through tmux session `spore`; log at `/tmp/opencode/spore-server.log`.
- Browser session used: `playwright-cli -s=spore`; Chromium headless shell installed.
- Test save currently exists in browser localStorage and loads a Generation 2 Prowler with den/mate/heir; use `#btn-new` or clear localStorage for fresh-start tests.
- `Game.panel` prevents simulation updates; panels are effectively paused. `openPanel`/`closePanel` drive all modal UI.
- `drawMapCanvas` uses `world.mapBase` + `mapTmp` fog overlay; explored cells stored in `Game.explored` as `cy * 100 + cx`.
- `this.heirPreview` is intentionally reset when closing the breed panel, on gene purchases, and after breeding.
